subject: How Trump is using DOJ to influence the midterms
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
So many of the attacks on voting this year come down to Trump's ego. He'll never let himself believe he legitimately lost in 2020, and he is absolutely terrified of a Congress controlled by the same party he has labeled as "traitors" and so much worse.
He seems willing to do anything -- and we mean anything -- to suppress votes, kill mail-in ballots, and drive people away from the polls.
We're working nonstop to defend our fundamental right to vote from a hostile administration and opponents of voting rights around the country. RUSH $35 or more today to fuel that work and make every vote count in the midterms and beyond! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041926_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Politico: Trump administration subpoenaing Arizona 2020 voting records, as Trump pushes to consolidate election power [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041926_2&amount=25]
Team: The Trump administration has subpoenaed records related to the 2020 election in Maricopa County, which is Arizona's largest county.
The move came just six weeks after the FBI raided an elections office outside Atlanta, seizing records related to the 2020 presidential election. This is because Trump and his cronies continue to spread debunked conspiracy theories about voter fraud in that election.
Arizona’s Maricopa County — like Georgia’s Fulton County — has long been a centerpiece of those conspiracy theories, with opponents of voting rights alleging widespread fraud in the 2020 election without evidence , even after multiple taxpayer-funded state investigations have found nothing.
Trump's MAGA DOJ is partly doing this to salve Trump's wounded ego over his 2020 loss. But they are also doing this to scare eligible voters away from participating in the crucial 2026 midterm elections.
Team: We must not let them silence our voices, especially at the ballot box. Help fuel our work to inform voters and protect our fundamental rights with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041926_2&amount=35]
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=041926_2&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=041926_2&amount=25]

GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=041926_2&amount=250] Other Amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041926_2&amount=35]
Trump has repeatedly threatened to “nationalize” elections ahead of the 2026 midterms, despite the fact that the Constitution explicitly delegates election administration duties to the states.
Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes had a strong response:
“ What the Trump administration appears to be pursuing now is not a legitimate law enforcement inquiry ,” Mayes said. “ It is the weaponization of federal law enforcement in service of crackpots and lies. ”
The "why" is patently clear -- make as many threats as possible in purple states and key districts to scare off eligible voters and suppress them before they even try and take part in the ballot process.
Overturning the 2020 results would be a bonus for MAGA, winning November's midterms is the real objective. Chip in $35 or however much you can to help us Inform and turn out as many eligible voters as possible and make each of those votes count >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041926_2&amount=35]
https://voteractionproject.org/ [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=041926_2&amount=20]

name: JusticeDemocrats.com
subject: An update
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, this is a
long but important email. We hope you’ll read to the end.

Last week, Israel carried out its largest airstrike campaign in Lebanon,
targeting densely populated residential neighborhoods in broad daylight
while Lebanese families were picking up their children from school.

The Israeli government did this right after the U.S. agreed to a ceasefire
with Iran, because the truth is, they don’t want this war to end.

Israel has been bombing and bulldozing entire villages in the south of
Lebanon, while keeping up its occupation of Gaza and the West Bank. Its
goal was always clear: colonial annexation.

U.S. leaders, including the Democratic establishment, let Israel get away
with bombing and starving Palestinians for two and a half years,
conducting genocide and ethnic cleansing in Gaza with the help of our tax
dollars. Now, it’s no surprise they’re applying the same playbook to
Lebanon with zero repercussions.

But voters are tired of it. A new nationwide poll reveals that 80% of
Democrat and independent voters hold unfavorable views of Israel.

Despite this, the DNC blocked a resolution to condemn the right-wing
megadonor-funded Israel lobby group, AIPAC, and we still have Senate
Minority Leader Chuck Schumer claiming his job is to “fight for aid to
Israel,” instead of fighting for the people he was elected to serve.

Too many AIPAC-backed Democrats are actively supporting Israel’s war
crimes. Many more are silent, while others give weak condemnations as they
keep voting to send Israel billions.

The people of this country are making it clear: we demand that the
Democratic Party unequivocally oppose any additional military aid and
weapons transfers to Israel as long as they continue their genocide and
ethnic cleansing.

Justice Democrats have stood on the right side of this since the
beginning, from Cori Bush introducing the original Gaza ceasefire
resolution to Saikat Chakrabarti taking the next step and calling for
sanctions.

These are the kinds of anti-war progressive leaders we can and must elect
in the upcoming Democratic primary elections, but as we take on AIPAC and
the rest of the corporate-backed establishment, we can’t win without your
support.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260419.6iFnJM&refcode=em20260419-37686&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37686%2E1203867%2EBRYXic ]Please, if you can, pitch in $5 to help us send a dozen
anti-AIPAC, pro-peace Justice Democrats to Congress this year to transform
the Democratic Party and stop the U.S. from enabling genocide and ethnic
cleansing any longer.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260419.6iFnJM&refcode=em20260419-37686&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1021&akid=37686%2E1203867%2EBRYXic ]Contribute $5

If do-nothing Democrats refuse to listen to their constituents and start
acting like the anti-war party they should be, we will force them out at
the ballot box.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2111%2E259176%2EBycDy-) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2111%2E259176%2EBycDy-)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11099?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.04.19_Troye-On-The-Line_B1_F1_S1_C1_tarsync_N-T1&t=4&akid=2111%2E259176%2EBycDy-) I've put everything on the line to speak out against Donald Trump and his far-right, enabling cronies. **I'm Olivia Troye. I'm the daughter of an immigrant and a truck driver who worked my way up to be one of the only women working in counterterrorism after being moved by the devastation of 9/11.** During my time at the Pentagon, I had a front row seat to _the chaos, the corruption, the calculated cruelty_ from the Trump administration. I pushed back when others wouldn’t. And when the dangers grew too great – I resigned. But I didn't go quietly. I've blown the whistle on MAGA for the illegal and unethical way they've "led" our country. And in return, I've received threats against my life and been dragged to court by Trump's attorneys. But here's the thing: **if I stay silent, that means their intimidation tactics worked. It means that their lawsuits and their death threats worked.** _So I've never backed down. We all remember the horrific ICE kidnapping and detention of five-year-old Liam Ramos, and so does Liam — his parents say he’s always worried about whether he’ll be taken again.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
His mom says Liam was once a happy and playful kid, but now he doesn’t want to play with other kids and shows signs of psychological trauma. He sees police officers and thinks they may be ICE agents coming to take him away.
It’s no wonder — armed and masked ICE agents literally took him from his driveway and shipped him to an inhumane detention center over a thousand miles away.
American taxpayers footed the bill for this, and it’s not OK.
Detaining and traumatizing children has nothing to do with fighting crime. 5-year-old Liam poses no threat to anyone. The cruelty has always been the point — and I will not stop fighting to end mass detention and shut down the horrific family detention centers that are profiting from human rights abuses.

What one violent incident reveals about crime in downtown Denver

**April 19, 2026** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
This week, one story out of downtown Denver captured the attention of readers across Colorado—and for good reason.
It was a real-world example of [what public safety looks like right now](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Earlier this month, a Denver man was randomly shot in the neck while riding a scooter near 18th and Stout after a brief encounter with passengers in an SUV.
According to the victim, Nico Francis, the interaction lasted seconds. A man in the vehicle shouted at him, pulled a gun, and later fired as the car drove away. Francis—an ICU respiratory therapist—knew immediately how serious the injury was. He began coughing up blood and losing function in his arm as he tried to find help.
At one point, he approached a vehicle at a stoplight and asked the driver to call 911. The driver left. He ultimately survived because a nearby bystander returned and applied pressure to the wound long enough for him to call for emergency services.
Doctors later said the bullet missed major arteries by millimeters.
The suspect was taken into custody shortly after the incident. But by the next day, he had [posted a $75,000 bond and was released with conditions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), including home confinement and GPS monitoring. Formal charges are still pending.
The victim survived—but the long-term impact is still unfolding. Francis is currently unable to use his right arm and faces an uncertain recovery timeline, with nerve damage affecting basic daily functions and his ability to work.
This story resonated because it highlights a broader concern many Coloradans have been raising: [Not just crime—but random, unpredictable crime.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Francis himself had been someone who regularly defended downtown Denver as safe. After the incident, he said he no longer feels that way. At the same time, he made clear he’s not calling for people to avoid the city—only that “something needs to change.”
That’s the tension Colorado continues to navigate. Public officials point to investments, reforms, and long-term strategies. But for many residents, stories like this shape perception far more than policy discussions do. Is the current approach working?
**If you haven’t read the full report, you can find it here:** ➡️ [He Loved This City. Then It Nearly Killed Him.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
In truth & liberty, Team RMV

GABE EVANS, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _TABOR, otherwise known as the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights, was created to protect Coloradans from bloated government spending, prevent politicians from overtaxing working families, and ensure extra revenue is returned to the people who earned it._

They left having done that—and still debating who should have a say in choosing them. What unfolded over the course of a long delayed and at times contentious assembly produced clear outcomes in major races while also setting in motion a legal step that could reshape how those candidates are selected in the future. __

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Marya Washburn is a federal Forest Service firefighter. At a January forum in Denver, Attorney General Phil Weiser singled her out by name as evidence of what his office has accomplished._

**LEGISLATIVE SESSION**
_**Quick Summary of the Week:**_ 🏛️ _**In the Senate:** The Senate took up the state budget, or _[“Long Bill,”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ this week—one of the most significant votes of the session—determining how taxpayer dollars will be spent. Senate Republicans pushed to increase funding for vulnerable populations while opposing what they described as unnecessary spending. Lawmakers also advanced bipartisan measures, including housing assistance for first responders and reforms to streamline charitable giving._
🏛️ _**In the House:** House lawmakers advanced a range of bills this week, including a win for rural communities with _[SB26-121](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ raising the overtime threshold for agricultural workers—an effort Republicans say restores flexibility for both workers and producers. Other measures moved on criminal law, child welfare, and regulation, while debate continued over _[SB26-005](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ , which critics argue could expand liability tied to immigration enforcement. Lawmakers also introduced resolutions supporting law enforcement and reaffirming TABOR, amid ongoing concerns about state spending and shrinking taxpayer refunds._ __
__📅**Coming Up This Week:**_The Capitol remains busy as lawmakers shift focus to advancing remaining bills on education, elections, energy, housing, and criminal justice. Key proposals on parental rights, TABOR, and ballot measures are scheduled for debate, while the Joint Budget Committee continues final adjustments to the state budget. With the session nearing its end, expect a fast-moving push on major legislation._[Click here if you're interested in testifying!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)__

GABE EVANS, TABOR, otherwise known as the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights, was created to protect Coloradans from bloated government spending, prevent politicians from overtaxing working families, and ensure extra revenue is returned to the people who earned it. BY JEN SCHUMANN, Colorado Republicans came to Pueblo to choose candidates. They left having done that—and still debating who should have a say in choosing them. What unfolded over the course of a long delayed and at times contentious assembly produced clear outcomes in major races while also setting in motion a legal step that could reshape how those candidates are selected in the future. BY SHAINA COLE, Marya Washburn is a federal Forest Service firefighter. She was fired by Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins last year, right before fire season. At a January forum in Denver, Attorney General Phil Weiser singled her out by name as evidence of what his office has accomplished. | LEGISLATIVE SESSION Quick Summary of the Week: 🏛️ In the Senate: The Senate took up the state budget, or this week—one of the most significant votes of the session—determining how taxpayer dollars will be spent. Senate Republicans pushed to increase funding for vulnerable populations while opposing what they described as unnecessary spending. Lawmakers also advanced bipartisan measures, including housing assistance for first responders and reforms to streamline charitable giving. 🏛️ In the House: House lawmakers advanced a range of bills this week, including a win for rural communities with raising the overtime threshold for agricultural workers—an effort Republicans say restores flexibility for both workers and producers. Other measures moved on criminal law, child welfare, and regulation, while debate continued over , which critics argue could expand liability tied to immigration enforcement. Lawmakers also introduced resolutions supporting law enforcement and reaffirming TABOR, amid ongoing concerns about state spending and shrinking taxpayer refunds. 📅Coming Up This Week:The Capitol remains busy as lawmakers shift focus to advancing remaining bills on education, elections, energy, housing, and criminal justice. Key proposals on parental rights, TABOR, and ballot measures are scheduled for debate, while the Joint Budget Committee continues final adjustments to the state budget. With the session nearing its end, expect a fast-moving push on major legislation. | The state Senate gave final approval Thursday to a new state budget. It came in at just under $47 billion, an increase of about $3 billion over last year. The discretionary portion of the budget — the general fund — is $17.4 billion. Tucked deep within the hundreds of pages of the proposed $46.8 billion 2026–27 state budget is a line item showing $306.1 million in savings — achieved by canceling TABOR refunds. Paid family leave. Wage transparency requirements. A lowered standard for harassment claims. BY JEN SCHUMANN, Colorado Republicans left Pueblo with more than a slate of candidates. They left with a plan to change who votes—and how soon that could happen. We now have our largest Colorado county (El Paso County) and a medium-sized county (Las Animas) using a commercial credit agency to flag registered voters who no longer reside at the address in SCORE. Timing is everything, especially in a close race like this.

Everyone is watching to see if we have the resources we’ll need to turn these polls into power — especially in a state as expensive and difficult to campaign in as Alaska.

And when my opponent and his dark money backers see these polls and realize that we have what it takes to win this Senate seat and take on the rigged DC system, they’re going to spend big to try and stop us.

That’s why we need a huge number of donations today to show everyone watching that we can and will win this fight for our future.

We only have one shot at this, so I’m counting on those of you who understand the importance of this moment to make a donation today before it’s too late. So I’m personally asking:

[Will you split a donation between the Voter Protection Project and my campaign for U.S. Senate? No matter how much you can afford to chip in today, it all adds up when lots of us are chipping in.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107394?t=9&akid=23759%2E878179%2EmIUHmr)

As long as we all work together, we will win Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat.

The strength of this campaign has always come from regular people stepping up when it counted. And it means a lot to me that so many of you have faith in our ability to win. Together, we’re building a movement.

Thanks for being a part of it.

\- Mary

| | | | | | Friends,
While Brad’s opponents engage in a "mutually assured destruction" of negative ads and mudslinging, Brad is focused on hardworking Georgians and their future.
A recent [article](https://BradForGeorgia.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cb0b5d8f4cac8238170f7992f&id=f49faa33cb&e=6036811227) from the Atlanta Journal Constitution highlights how the mudslinging between Burt Jones and Rick Jackson is ultimately cutting voters out of the conversation. This dynamic creates a clear path to victory for Brad. While Jones and Jackson split the vote with negativity, Brad is consolidating support by offering real solutions to lower costs, back law enforcement, and create jobs.

| Dear Friend,
**I was live on air when the Palm Beach Sheriff walked in.** No warning. No phone call. While my team and I were broadcasting to tens of thousands of people — a deputy came through the doors of OMG headquarters and handed me a restraining order. **Served live. On camera. For the world to see.** The person who filed it? **Matthew Tyrmand** — a former Project Veritas board member who [**admitted on hidden camera that he wants me dead.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NTJ9AAwAAAAAACP782nKCwQARnGlpsFoS2vSZe6GEt9co5X6CwOIP6s79fOSy1pR6_UMT3eX3FtSpqBo6obvdNJSTgXV2k8OsAC_sdaLErQbWxV1hJHXAw "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-served-on-air-hf/?utm_source=lg-omg-served-on-air&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=35") [****](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NTJ9AAwAAAAAACP782nLLzY6j4-tNCd-N2PcFTBQrNxJDTnjkerFezos01MCp7GIqVTQ-wyBUt03dM3hF7uMqruvUhm1KBbgJEeGCiKffLkbPIheH13_wA "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-served-on-air-hf/?utm_source=lg-omg-served-on-air&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=35") **Let that sink in.** The man who said he wants to murder me ran to a Miami courthouse and filed a domestic violence restraining order against **ME.** **And yesterday, it got worse.** I stood before a judge in Miami. He extended that restraining order **until May 11th.** And then he asked me to **surrender all of my firearms.** I'm a journalist. I operate in dangerous environments — Minneapolis mobs, government whistleblowers, cartel country. My security team carries firearms because **the threats against my life are real and documented.** **Now a court is trying to disarm me.** I need your help to fight this. Will you chip in **$35** to my legal defense fund right now? **** | [ DONATE TO JAMES'S LEGAL DEFENSE → ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NTJ9AAwAAAAAACP782nMU-qC4qCay5V6cCFs5Ouw0wTypr2E7ndLEYm7rrprz31fZMcx9m3WslKjGjrchXjjxmBbgZ6gmo0beIGTzUqId8X3mdgOMkdkKQ "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-served-on-air-hf/?utm_source=lg-omg-served-on-air&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=35")
---
Here's what you need to understand about why this is happening:
**We are winning.**
In the past year alone, OMG investigations have generated over **1 million YouTube views** , triggered a **$9 billion Treasury audit** , and led to **$253 million in federal contracts being suspended**. Our hidden camera footage of FBI and DOJ officials has exposed corruption at the highest levels of the United States government.
**They cannot beat us in the court of public opinion. So they're trying to beat us in an actual court.**
This restraining order isn't about domestic violence. [**It's about silencing an investigative journalist who has caught too many powerful people on camera.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NTJ9AAwAAAAAACP782nNJdAo7I1NvA-At08UlwPSt_dIqKWmKcw9dg3BVNLN1OSnkAsl9b8OQHuKKUZwK8oLlFqmLFpfkee9oUyP_mVkLjlxKmpQpu2fwA "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-served-on-air-hf/?utm_source=lg-omg-served-on-air&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=35") Matthew Tyrmand served on the Project Veritas board — the same board that ousted me, sued me, and has spent years trying to destroy everything I've built.
**Now they're using the legal system as a weapon.**
My legal team **filed an emergency interlocutory appeal today** challenging this order. We're fighting back on every front — First Amendment, Second Amendment, due process. All of it.
**But legal battles like this cost real money. And right now, we need your help.**
**$35** helps cover one hour of my attorneys' time fighting this appeal.
**$50** funds the constitutional research behind our emergency motion.
**$100** covers court filing fees and legal review.
**$250 or more** helps us keep fighting this all the way to the top — and fund the next investigation while we do it.
**They want me disarmed, silenced, and tied up in court while they continue to operate in the dark.**
**I'm not letting that happen.**
****
[ CHIP IN $35 TO MY LEGAL DEFENSE NOW → ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NTJ9AAwAAAAAACP782nO5iD3QfQcbOZeYw5O1mVvMmQWkoUDaPOdirudzZIWhOeKbpLmr-oVjgZUDy1EF8hOhkeaxj44SQG84dHFRcTpcIAXDyCFvFhHHg "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-served-on-air-hf/?utm_source=lg-omg-served-on-air&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=35")
---
You and I both know that if they can do this to me — served live on national television, stripped of my right to bear arms, buried under legal fees — **they can do it to any journalist who dares expose them.**
**This isn't just about me. It's about whether truth-telling journalism survives in this country.**
I've been through the raid on the journalist who had the Ashley Biden diary. I've been through Project Veritas suing me after throwing me out. I've been through the mob in Minneapolis who gave me **one hour to leave or be killed.**
**I didn't leave then. I'm not leaving now.**
But I need you in this fight with me.
Please give your most generous gift today — **$35, $100, $250** , or whatever you can — to the **O'Keefe Legal Defense Fund** hosted by Liberty Guard. Every dollar goes directly to fighting this unconstitutional order and keeping our cameras rolling.

And right now, we need your help. $35 helps cover one hour of my attorneys' time fighting this appeal. $50 funds the constitutional research behind our emergency motion. $100 covers court filing fees and legal review. $250 or more helps us keep fighting this all the way to the top — and fund the next investigation while we do it. They want me disarmed, silenced, and tied up in court while they continue to operate in the dark. I'm not letting that happen. "" You and I both know that if they can do this to me — served live on national television, stripped of my right to bear arms, buried under legal fees — they can do it to any journalist who dares expose them. This isn't just about me. It's about whether truth-telling journalism survives in this country. I've been through the raid on the journalist who had the Ashley Biden diary. I've been through Project Veritas suing me after throwing me out. I've been through the mob in Minneapolis who gave me one hour to leave or be killed. I didn't leave then. I'm not leaving now. But I need you in this fight with me. Please give your most generous gift today — $35, $100, $250 , or whatever you can — to the O'Keefe Legal Defense Fund hosted by Liberty Guard. Every dollar goes directly to fighting this unconstitutional order and keeping our cameras rolling. "" In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder and CEO O'Keefe Media Group P.S. A former Project Veritas board member — a man who said on hidden camera he wants me dead — just got a judge to order me to surrender my firearms. I filed an emergency appeal today. The hearing is May 11th. If you've ever believed in what we're doing, I need you now. "" ""

---
| | Friend,
The Democratic Party has made its choice: [Washtenaw County Prosecutor Eli Savit is their choice for Attorney General.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001A8TUzS-kW9gL2ygKfm62lekFtatBQIpNCuWZStK7rP4jtERjwQ17h0xZw4nNYppyevkDgGFmHsLOohQ_rAqaEd5Tv6ZjkrSXtQqqa67Ki_q63G2Fh13xHpUmmhCQ8iiXXeNasarQSvvQAWoIfAQ4N99o5ASG_9IIubugSzug76L3nyD_IJ-oN7TRjl2O5eCPLJdXXLOtGFkv6moOrW7BUY0IHdLXmcfR2Ri-xldaXCvECQAsAEs02DaOIeTagUDcQ8fkD4tiM6wkmBL5beOw016Xo351TBWcUlyK1CfE_yavMc5DmDAxv5mFNKsm9JzD1a857n6_SpE=&c=VnEZ7_PhFQmL62uZRvUS3wbG-S6hdfrtq542R61nCMMyK94QxciSnA==&ch=8wtEjCx1gIiV2hH3OFzFnbJOeMfGSeA09mDLs6zQQ0_rNuXzOEuWag==)
I want to be clear about something right from the start. I welcome this race. I look forward to a healthy debate that gives Michigan voters a clear contrast on our beliefs, our records, and our vision for this office.
Because that contrast could not be more important.
In just the past few days, [reports have shown](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001A8TUzS-kW9gL2ygKfm62lekFtatBQIpNCuWZStK7rP4jtERjwQ17h0xZw4nNYppy_Fe4tyiNBzC0z5F37VYb3Dj6htlF4kkLnFsVvuevH6w_vPTeTLB0h7_MhN0OeVxlRAz--DphOG0fVcNWojcVxS9h3rCy0frBOR51hH1na3soBRb_syxEzLAvwEur4FMTPjc3C6m9pP1zVj4Mld7LDD0ABaBaFNkEgNPwLVJ43vfxucwrCByTjFQORFvWmj0YkAT4AuVsNieJrL76l3JayVUtQ7_5Xgk-XVQAdpeyYd-qagwxTgxfMRZ38OkrSsu_xJFmCr1jFAc5B9vs0GrEVw==&c=VnEZ7_PhFQmL62uZRvUS3wbG-S6hdfrtq542R61nCMMyK94QxciSnA==&ch=8wtEjCx1gIiV2hH3OFzFnbJOeMfGSeA09mDLs6zQQ0_rNuXzOEuWag==) that Mr. Savit used taxpayer-funded resources, including a government gas card, to cover travel tied to his campaign for higher office.
That is not a gray area. That is a mindset.
Public office is a public trust. Taxpayer dollars are not a personal expense account.
I have spent my career as a prosecutor understanding that responsibility. As Attorney General, I will be a careful and accountable steward of every dollar entrusted to that office, because it belongs to the people of Michigan, not the politicians who temporarily hold power.
But here is the reality we are facing.
Mr. Savit will have the full backing of a well-funded political machine, national donors, and a network that knows how to protect its own.
We are not going to outspend them.
We are going to outwork them, [but we still need the resources to compete.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001A8TUzS-kW9gL2ygKfm62lekFtatBQIpNCuWZStK7rP4jtERjwQ17hzz4KIa8hIctjbYYlWUMyWkyoJ9cEeLwPJxb1TI0Pip5HeWchE6F3iwK9mzI-Z20fThhWj7zkd78RzaoytJcE01vTRrm7kJU1XoFqhFhyzfqbXLhKmdWYxRotvpRRMOrAFUx8ZbLjnFmXzhnq2aBZ8hHvkQwYFLHb1swfaNivYsG&c=VnEZ7_PhFQmL62uZRvUS3wbG-S6hdfrtq542R61nCMMyK94QxciSnA==&ch=8wtEjCx1gIiV2hH3OFzFnbJOeMfGSeA09mDLs6zQQ0_rNuXzOEuWag==)
[That means building a campaign strong enough to reach voters across Michigan, share this message, and make sure people understand what is at stake in this election.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001A8TUzS-kW9gL2ygKfm62lekFtatBQIpNCuWZStK7rP4jtERjwQ17hzz4KIa8hIctjbYYlWUMyWkyoJ9cEeLwPJxb1TI0Pip5HeWchE6F3iwK9mzI-Z20fThhWj7zkd78RzaoytJcE01vTRrm7kJU1XoFqhFhyzfqbXLhKmdWYxRotvpRRMOrAFUx8ZbLjnFmXzhnq2aBZ8hHvkQwYFLHb-t_ZOXRuOMx&c=VnEZ7_PhFQmL62uZRvUS3wbG-S6hdfrtq542R61nCMMyK94QxciSnA==&ch=8wtEjCx1gIiV2hH3OFzFnbJOeMfGSeA09mDLs6zQQ0_rNuXzOEuWag==)

| Peter,
Patriots' Day reminds us of the courage and sacrifice that shaped the very beginning of our nation. On April 19, 1775, ordinary citizens answered the call at Lexington and Concord, standing for liberty and self-government against impossible odds.
Here in Maine, we also remember the spirit of that fight in places like Machias, where patriots defended freedom off the coast of present-day Washington County.
Today, we honor those who came before us by exemplifying the values they fought so hard for-- faith, freedom, community, and the enduring belief that government should answer to the people.
Rep. Mike Soboleski Proudly Serving House District 73

## 8 Children Killed in Louisiana Shooting
A 31-year-old Army veteran fatally shot eight children, including seven of his own, during a rampage across three Shreveport, Louisiana, homes early Sunday morning. The victims [ranged in age from 3 to 11](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQgOGnwRvWBTC2B4Yu3tK1o0XgHF-FIQJiK29fuWr7At1-6aQ7ffdxna-WAsX7u93Q1CXNEY8SsFbMc0hPKmSj3WwpZU2pUrxXqnYWIDQHxQXM3lJ4zarxZkEUKBs0l77Xuh87rZrVqK7vxnHolNdgAWGxDuyib-rihbBSNmTObaAEXAA0yLYfxkE6dEqNi1M3zxSgp5py-5ko1hWX8Eo75talrQlmrfVRmHxjYmJiOo6jjTd3Ks45E9OZTEzPwn_qj8XLmnHHR8qVn0T-a-TZRSsVDHposvGPg0Kgonum4L5ZCt-X67_etRvxFQAA__82-oBh). Most of the children were shot in the head while they slept. Police said the eighth child appeared to have tried to escape from the back roof of the house before [being shot](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdI7M4PBTuNjGXbbdEhl7gNkYjOxJorz9FZHufYHbzkhH3zn_buPNUaR9-es2NDynccdXiciMeYzpQYXc7jZXSllTYtoXJnYjKGil0hLUGBzF96irYGZEwKZCU3dd23bDtdXVasAp7Jpp0J2f5mvfeBVaB9pdsR_QT1iROWlKg6qValVz6fqhbzx6rYfZ6ykIrTAQp3z5n2jnFef4Tk_MF5-2KpqV-Sii-SPACrD7-0iFz5cAe4IFWKUF2HoQYB9Fnn4CbC_vFIp0CxZZS06y1vJOMWKQtMtTWH4bF-l8Tp9DxiceKbP8SSPAVtmE40UxUmk7odWyOYqfcfyrok8DXwEAAP__Qi6K1w). The gunman also shot the two mothers of his children, each in the head. Both survived, one with life-threatening injuries. A relative told reporters the gunman and his wife were in the process of separating and were due in court on Monday. The pair had been arguing about the separation when [he opened fire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu3CAQheGnwR0rPGCzLijSuLtpU1oYxmYSbCyYu9a-fbR5hdRH-nT0__pavjxlOvef_kDHW1lOvFtGZqxLLt_UyJ_-8K21VArTuTOxX0DBKJWRoJboKb8X00W3IQLqDl1v7TjaaRhNl5zxk7bWrBDXAfpNaz3CMFkVVwjPOKiO3EdTBlSv1Kj0wz6npw4YjJm2YNYojMJIXOrjd6GTE275XV5YH6EcXXaJ-WpC_xAwC5jv-378adl_RgHzhxYwKyNg7icBM9KeWLZU8YVXqSxDohwrnjKij9JvjFXeybNccfenjOXAxhRkpHZ9M8qrZAoom38LmLvq4nVTztRGK4zaD0_53y_-r5gvB38DAAD__xr8iRo). The gunman fled, carjacked a vehicle, and was shot dead by police in neighboring Bossier City after a chase.
## Iran Rejects New Talks, Strait Stays Shut
Iran on Sunday [rejected a second round of peace talks](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQRp_GdEazxmugcJGG7qZNiYw9u0ziH2QPizZPH21e4daf9Omc8-tr_XIUKT9_uoSWH2XNeLWIzFjXWE5q5LJLrrW2l8KUn0zsVgXKSNBSwRocxfequ2AfiAqHDu1tHI0Z57vR3W6N3u7DZAKOfoNx8vcNQG-AWm-zV5PpyH7eQCu4ARgY-nGap8Gj13p-eL0FoQEDcan970KZd3zEd3lh7X1JXbQ789HE8EOoRajluq6ecsADc8DMvS_9-Ueo5aP1mUuNQaglUQgRJbrGQi1UXZZnk5erMtILZePqiOVeajr_Sq5nOiS16jDK8wiOsclNzQbuN-h3TrGrNhwXxUjNjELDMzmK__n4W1FfVv0LAAD__0HbjdQ) with the United States, citing "excessive demands, unrealistic expectations, constant shifts in stance, repeated contradictions, and the ongoing naval blockade," according to Iran's official state news agency, even as a U.S. delegation prepared to travel to Islamabad on today. The rejection came after [President Trump threatened to destroy](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGngS2RfRw2HjxUqtjSqVJH5OIjXGUwsi-J8vZV-gpdv0_6Df-vy3QJnHi_foSNvCx52ulRE4lQmVK-ceWwhy3UWtechfersIQJFJiTwhOoKQZOzwnb6BcioK4lr601xrreYLv66JAW3dGsexV7s4DFQbtODWE2dnHYsn9pCkFppYzqznZwQzfTjOiWGb9jg4oiSy7nn8y7rLSkZ75TOc95a5NfRY7adG8NjA2MUm6y1jxzSK__NaIqFNJ73kOKn-W2HQ2MR65SGxi1NthpcLa3DixYa9vi4_HglLga26C6boH_qFb-1efu4TcAAP__dBx3qQ) every power plant and bridge in Iran if Tehran doesn't accept a deal before the fragile two-week ceasefire expires Wednesday. Vice President JD Vance, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner are still expected to travel to Pakistan for the talks. Iran reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, one day after declaring the waterway open, with merchant vessels [reporting gunfire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiNjfMAEDi6ZbC69EDXuNu6VsZHtGTT79StW-wcblVQllare_8fyAA4ct3-wk6kuLZHOEqhWyktITy4MEXYopfiUKsetcoVFSTUKqYWSCwKH96JbNI5I0dCS6adpHKfbn1G33ljCecW1h6EHdAi4EqlerTjZvndOtWyuNqmV7KUc5dBN820eLFmtb87qFRstCbmm3H0kjtWTC-_0otzZtLfB-FqP0gx_G3Vv1P08zy6u9npx5ZeTcsBG3TlD_BGBXCpES-IgsCSQIAif8v78FDak8swkPIRaRPF8HBw3kW2EQctZj202eJwcApdxarTcduDwvaX-CuDLqK8AAAD__39giJk) from Iranian gunboats.
## Titanic Life Jacket Sells for $906K
A life jacket worn by a first-class passenger as she escaped the sinking _Titanic_ sold at auction in Devizes, England, on Saturday for $906,000, nearly double the estimated price. [See the life jacket here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGPozAUhH8NdEYvtmNw4eIaulx7JTL2I7ycsRE8gvLvV2y39ZajGY3mm3-P4eEpUX7-9Qs6nsqQ8dwTMuM2pHLQTj77xe_7PpfClJ9M7AcJ0gjQQsIQPaXPoOvoJkSJqkZ3a1tjWns3up5dNKoDBXa8y9GGMXZaKxvsBGaM1iioyV1toCXcAAyopu1spwIGre0U9BgrDRiJy9a8CmWecUqf8satCWWpk5uZ171SfyrZV7I_z7PJY7goLr-S_VpWEY7Ex4Y_lbhClewTTShePvxHFhddpiD8EZhKxii2kL3S0N1Uvbm4npQS7aatNDwXT-l7BP_qubeTXwEAAP__t8OEGw). The cork-filled canvas preserver was worn by Laura Mabel Francatelli, a 31-year-old secretary traveling with fashion designer Lucy Duff Gordon. After the rescue, Francatelli and seven other survivors from Lifeboat No. 1 signed the jacket, which launched with just 12 people on board despite having room for 40. It was the only life jacket from a _Titanic_ survivor ever offered at auction. A lifeboat seat cushion sold at the same event for $527,000 to the owners of [Titanic museums](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAQRb8GdxgsEWTBYjbu3ltN0ktDY9FWD4oR1PTfT5zMH7xlpVKn7rmPr_HLUaT19e0WtCWkccUrRywF9zGmgzK51S0u5zynVGh9FSpuBAGKC8lBjJOj-BllNdmACNhWaButldKmU7KabY-qgaA9KGMw9OqpAxr57ELXYKs0VGRvmpAgGiGUaGvdm7716KU0wcvnxKTAiUra63eitcwY4ieduNc-LVW0cylbZu0vBgOD4bqu-tjo3jEYfqdt_MYrMxgeaY8T_z_cHxkMQjIYmp7BcFut5HmkgPzt_B8sPB_7SWfaeU5x4u7whdJ6HyhzG3Zd15gbUO122i6KkbLSTIrX4ij-C1d-1Ohp4W8AAAD__xQYiAM) in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, and Branson, Missouri. The _Titanic_ struck an iceberg on April 14, 1912, during its maiden voyage from England to New York. About 1,500 of the 2,200 passengers and crew died.

## Energy Demand Forecast Likely Inflated
Officials with the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), the state's power grid operator, met with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) on Friday to discuss ERCOT's recent report projecting that the state's energy demand will [quadruple](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFyhCAQBuCn0Q4HFwEtKNLYXdqUzp4sHhMUA9x59_YZL4-Qboudf_7v_7pMF_TBb8snrmTK08VpoyMHKoXSRGmOxdKKm3Ux0Yy5wIIZtwk4KMY7Bnyy6MNr6mprrtwObU2m1VqpXvBW1zfTo3S9lNo5wGEQfct1rwS_Dko5EIC1N2cY74C3LRdCNs7KYZad1gSt0FJWHSfrS0xNuVGhJ2YXXvFBqZnjWgdzK2XPlfioYKxgPI6jcfHZnYzzoYLxPCsY3xq2J7J-LpntMWd_DcR2wm_2p2Q_d7TpvgdiwAUwiwXZTFuhlNmS4lEnY_fDh-Cz0lXHlxV9ePco_1vvYeA3AAD__9MLhJ0) over the next six years. A [report](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOwyAQRU-DO1vDACYpKLZxl223RASGBAmbCFCc3H4Va2-w9RvNf___XOzFpZy227dbyfRXLHajvWXqnaql6ksPtLotxFLJu9bx5prbLALOI8gRwQaX8tvKIZgrhDMfyHCt5_kkgOvhbsIMgvtZIMVAPga8eu0FnCQKiqhgSObzDCQC5yCEmmJQZ6-k1oRcaKWYBAqplzr1O3V6uRbzuzypTr6sQzb33h-NiS-GC8Nl3_fp8P5QhsunDsOlUibXiOECkqtD_7ga_0AbH5VyWtPm6nuoJjz2lHNqs2YSbqtL-Ujr_9voafA3AAD__wAies0) submitted last week predicts peak energy demand will reach 367,790 megawatts by 2032, while the all-time record from August 2023 is 85,508 megawatts. However, ERCOT President and CEO Pablo Vegas said the forecast is likely inflated due to the "changing landscape" of the state's data center boom. "_Texas is experiencing exceptional growth and development, which is reshaping how large load demand is identified, verified, and incorporated into long-term planning_ ," [Vegas said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unTAUhFdjOl_5D8wtXKShe2lTooN9AOsZg-yTB-w-4m4h9Wg-zTd_vsYviCnm5Tds6Oia9zHjWRMSYRmx-J0CbpDDvBf0UEktUCGPSqiOC8OVGAPEdI-mCW4S4S0bdNLaruu1kLZZnentFDxIo8G8ZS-ndjJTK3ptdWcs9k10D0wYJaQUWrevObRv3xprUUlt25YZgSHSXl60IuEFdU73_oPl5fetSW4lOirTv5gamBrO83x9X5CfkKnhsWFq-NSYGj5G_CgYoqfKzcUPhG-OGcty878VFuTTzZXQiq_7yQMQcI-ZsFS-wc3jdoAnTmvMywNsigvHGVOKtbPMiGWDmD7D6P_u_HHqXwAAAP__T4WJqw). Texas is expected to become the country's No. 1 data center market within two years. The PUCT ordered ERCOT to reevaluate its forecast to ensure accuracy before it's used to make long-term plans. "_I think it's clear we need to engage in the process to find ways to refine this number into something that's more usable_ ," PUCT Chair Thomas Gleeson [said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1y5CAQhU-DMqagQcITEGxC5k03VPVAS6KMxBS0R57bb423fIKN--e97_vzPr9jLvlYf-NOnr-WOh909kLM1GZqsXKiHY-01EYRO8OKHY8ZFExSWQlqTpjLc7ZD8jeVrnogr52bpjejtBs2n7RGC9HEhVy8mWmcbtHqqxmJyJg3PWT_eqYsKK2VMeNlSeM1jtY5Am3cOAqrKGWu7cIbMX1hX8qzPqhdYt2H4jfmexfml4AgIJzneYklxw_Y6mfnery2BIQXloDwfS8gvDIFBGUFBO1-BnJtOcl6p4Zcm_yB7nLH3vOD5NrqyZvMh_ynRd4-WXZ8dpmQUeYuS_6g8pRLwZOSgDA0n-5nLiX3yQmr1h1z-W7O_-f74eFvAAAA__8W6JV_).
## Fermi America CEO Steps Down
Toby Neugebauer, the CEO of the Rick Perry-backed company developing the world's largest data center campus near Amarillo, [stepped down](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQgOGnsTdbcICJB4Yu3tK1o3UxR4wEJoJTnLx9lb5C51_6hv_nul4xpnjcvzGT41co60FnS8RMdaW6FfaU8fChVNqwMdyx4bGCgGkQegCxeozpvereu5vws-zJSWun6aKEtP3uMKAJxiNNhm7zNF-slnQBC6SttML00X0woUFIKZQyY_Bm3oy2lkAqa0ynBfnIpY68E9MLW0jv8qQ6biX3ye3Mj9aprw6WDpbzPEcs6dM6WLBy3BK1DpZANccBM9W44bBRGRrTow2-nMcgZjUrO4Mad86pr84_zphSbJPttLhnjH9iz_979HTwGwAA__-eaHoF) Friday, causing Fermi America's stock to plummet more than 30% in aftermarket trading. The endeavor, dubbed Project Matador, was announced last June, and Fermi America went public in October. In December, a prospective tenant canceled a $150 million advance to support construction, prompting investors to [file](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3upCAUBfCnwQ7Dl_K3oNjGbrbd0lzhoiQIBphxfPuN-wrbn_xyzvnzWl4QYkjbbzjQtK_PS8KrRmwNy4LF5ubwgOR8LmihNrFBhbQIJkbKFBVscRDivajOmZW5iXdouNbj-CMZ191u5MiVnVYhx9XZCRXjk1fiZ0CvHSLYLpgHY0owzpmUQ-_dMNlBaY2CSz0MRDF0oeXStx0bfqH6eOcPlt7mo4tmb-2sRP4iYiZivq6rd9DAYmpY3J3gCLY-USJmTETMz0AiZo_lCDQkW6nFTFteb5rwveEKbyy0NjwrdflKtO5QsFIPMVLJ6InlwYmYu2LceYUYQx01UWw7IMR_rdr_ffkx4m8AAAD__29Hiok) a class-action lawsuit. In a Thursday interview, Neugebauer [acknowledged](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAUhE8DmVv-A9OBg07IZtMN0Wv7Ad71D2u_GaZvv6KvMFFJVapS6fv9sXxAiCFvvyChpe-1LBnPFpEI64LVFfKYIPu1VHTQSG7QIC-Sy5FxzSRfPIT4WnTv7ZP7u-jRCmPGcVJcmH63KMQT1X2cNJ_EJAbkDoxTelQaAZzqg73GuJZcCK7UcFv9cHeDNgalUGYYOs3RByr1RjsSfkNb46t8Yb25kvpod6KjderRybmT83met9TylXVyxsw-WyfnVDK-LoX6F-lyqH6mgz0rZI-eQWAeCJjDTFhZwg2OWv6gI9YIYmzMYWEeD6jvNlT2eEiB_3boq_XHGWIMbTSd5luCEN_X6GdAv6z8HwAA___nWYsD) that he "misunderstood where the supply chain is" for the equipment needed to cool advanced AI chips. He said the company was in talks with a prospective tenant but couldn't disclose who. Fermi America plans to power the 11-gigawatt data center with on-site solar, natural gas, and nuclear power. Project Matador is being developed on 5,236 acres leased from Texas Tech University and could eventually expand to 7,570 acres.
## BJ's Wholesale Club Launches in Texas
Massachusetts-based BJ's Wholesale Club [will open](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOwyAUBNDT2J0t-MaQFBTbuMu2W1of-LZZYbCAxMntV8kVth2Nnkbzc5tv6IOP6zfupOtzSXOkswSqlfJM2abqaMfolpTJYqmwYsE4AwPZMdEBmx368JpF67Rh7spb0lwpKS8D46rd9NWisUZxZqQlPjiy7oIgwEgcL4Bj6_UbYwIY52wYxn5x49WOQikCPqhxbAQj52vKfd2o0hPLEl7pQbm3aW-D3mo9SjN8NTA1MJ3n2e-vghFjTdGnd6mBydyLj1RKAxPm6m2gd_hbunNLgQoG6my4m-7jd-mg6OPaAQAHLkV_bEebtTtOH4IvUjWCrTv68JlQ_3fcQ8NfAAAA__989INO) its first Texas store in Forney this Friday and plans to open locations in Fort Worth, Grand Prairie, and Waxahachie in the coming weeks. subject: Brian Babin Endorses Jon Bonck for TX-38!
body:
| | | | |

| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Date: April 20, 2026 Contact: william@jonbonck.com
Congressman Brian Babin Endorses Jon Bonck for TX-38, Becomes 10th Member of Texas Delegation to Back Campaign HOUSTON, TX -- Congressman Brian Babin has endorsed Jon Bonck for Congress in Texas' 38th Congressional District, becoming the tenth member of the Texas delegation to get behind the campaign.
"Texas' 38th District is home to the Energy Corridor and some of the hardest working families in our state. Jon Bonck understands what it takes to keep that engine running strong. He's ready to support American energy, grow our economy, and represent TX 38 with integrity. I'm proud to endorse him," said Babin.
"I'm really grateful to have Congressman Babin's support," said Jon Bonck. "He's been a strong voice for Texas and someone who has consistently stood up for our values. It means a lot to have him in our corner as we keep building this campaign across TX 38."
Babin's endorsement is the latest sign of growing support from leaders across Texas. Bonck has now earned the backing of ten members of the Texas delegation, including U.S. Senator Ted Cruz and Congressmen Morgan Luttrell, Brandon Gill, Lance Gooden, Ronny Jackson, Pete Sessions, Jodey Arrington, Roger Williams, and Pat Fallon.
Entering the runoff with a commanding lead after receiving 47 percent of the vote in a 10 candidate field, Jon Bonck's momentum continues to grow as more leaders and voters across TX 38 rally behind his campaign.

Defend Our Courts helped power back-to-back Democratic landslides in the Pennsylvania and Wisconsin Supreme Court races.
In those races, we highlighted the dire consequences that Democrats would face if they lost--a full-out assault by Trump & MAGA to rig the elections in those states.
But with the Georgia Supreme Court race next month, the situation is different. Unlike PA and WI, Democrats currently do not hold a majority on the court. And what Georgia Democrats have had to endure at the hands of a MAGA controlled state Supreme Court proves what we've been saying all along:

| But we have good news: Democrats have a chance to launch a counteroffensive against Trump's election rigging plot in Georgia next month.
On May 19, Democrats have a shot at flipping two seats on the Georgia Supreme Court.
This race is the mirror image of Wisconsin. But this time, Democrats are the ones on offense.
Right now, MAGA holds a crushing 9-0 stranglehold on the court. Flip these two seats and that becomes 7-2 and suddenly a path opens up to reclaim the court entirely.
3 more seats are up for grabs in May 2028. Win these two seats next month, and Democrats could flip this critical swing state court to a 5-4 majority in '28 -- just months before the presidential election.

Hello, I hope the spring is going well for you! Kind of feels like we skipped a season.
I spoke at the University at Albany last week and met with a number of students. They were bright and thinking about their future. A couple of them said they wanted to go to law school.
I responded, "If you go, try to find an inexpensive way to get your degree. I'm not sure the numbers will work out." We went through the math. Maybe $80k a year for tuition, room and board. Times 3 = $240,000 in debt. How much would you have to make for that to make sense - and would that job be waiting for them in 4 years? I was openly dubious but didn't want to be a jackass raining on their ambition. It's good that they even had an ambition, after all.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/44d92652-db51-47f9-b580-7a03440c2937?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But it left me thinking about just how rough it's going to be for the next generation.
"Things have gotten so much worse in the last 10 years." This is what the CEO of a major AI-enabled company said to me this week. His company has tripled its revenue in the last few years. But he's cutting staff and sounding the alarm about AI. "The truth is, the faster we replace people, the better we will do." He's for a negative income tax to give people a floor paid for by AI-fueled profits.
His summary of the situation in three words: "With the help of AI, capital displaces labor."
That's actually the best distillation of the moment we're in.
Also this idea: "The easiest people to fire are those you haven't hired yet." It's one reason why college students are going into the most unwelcoming job market in a generation.
I [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/164c2fed-5237-4cd1-8dd0-74bcc426645a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week about unemployed and underemployed college graduates. I said in 2019 "coders will definitely be automated." I knew that was the case because what coders do is highly structured and rules-based, sort of like the corporate law contracts I reviewed in my twenties, and I knew that highly structured rules-based work would be catnip for AI.
"A lot of corporate workers are there to maintain a legacy system or manage a project that isn't core to the company's work," a tech executive commented to me. "Maybe 25% are touching something vital to what the company is doing right now." That leaves 75% scrambling to justify their role. The [end of the office](https://substack.com/redirect/99776bdc-7673-4af0-bb67-86515da71a62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) will be painful.
"AI is going to push millions of people up or down a class. People don't take that well." That's what an AI executive said to me over dinner.
Capitalism plus AI will be no one's idea of a good time.
I'm pretty sure the numbers will show that entrepreneurship is going to rise, simply because there will be a ton of unemployed college grads and techies and others and they'll have no choice. I love entrepreneurship as it can bring out the best in people. But for every successful startup, there will be 9 or 10 failures. Starting a business is not for everyone, and this environment will be unforgiving as the work gets stripped away.
The footwear company Allbirds pivoted to AI and its stock popped 700%. Maybe your shoes will tell you that your feet stink.
The water level is going to rise quickly. Appreciate what you've got, build a boat as best you can and try to bring others in.
You know something we can all do better on? Our data. Go to [noblemobile.com/yang](https://substack.com/redirect/8b8a1fc8-b295-4ae8-80a8-68e320f17292?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for 3 months off your wireless bill, the best deal around that will also reduce your screen time and help you save for your family. Email [matt@noblemobile.com](https://substack.com/redirect/d86c5a6c-d635-4400-ad25-2e9df5752ee1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to get a human being. A new study just came out showing that time off of Instagram and Facebook improves your mood dramatically. I interview Princeton neuroscientist turned Congressional candidate Sam Wang on the [podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/faa80fae-375e-4d36-a63e-4bd4a3a8b6f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this week. The [Hudson Valley Ideas Fest](https://substack.com/redirect/db6f964b-12a6-4a86-8205-ee5be585ab1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) returns to Rosendale, NY on April 25th. Go outside and look up.

body:

|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6532?source=&t=1&akid=1094%2E124072%2EY2kS4_)
| | | |
---
Normally when writing these emails, I try to approach them differently from the other political emails you’d typically get. Peter, this time is different, so I have to be more direct:
**[I’m reaching out today with a last-ditch request for a contribution of $5, or anything you can spare now.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/9338?t=8&akid=1094%2E124072%2EY2kS4_) That’s because the Senate GOP’s leading super PAC pledged to flood the North Carolina airwaves with $71 million in attack ads to lie about my record and keep this seat red. **
To be clear: It is not normal for the GOP to write such massive checks seven months out from Election Day.
This time, they know North Carolina is key to saving their majority. They know the polls show our opponent within striking distance. They will spare no expense to prop him up.
Though we knew these attacks were coming, we’re now facing way more outside spending _way earlier_ than we had expected. That means we’re going to have to ramp up our fundraising in order to fight back and set the record straight – and Peter, that’s where you come in:
**[While Republicans can easily direct their megadonors to drop tens of millions of dollars into this race, I’m relying on hundreds of thousands of folks like you – giving what you can, when you can – to compete in spite of their efforts to buy this seat out from under us. Now that you’re up to date, can I please count on you to chip in $5, $25 or anything you can spare right away to help me fight back?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/9339?t=9&akid=1094%2E124072%2EY2kS4_)**
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/9339?t=10&akid=1094%2E124072%2EY2kS4_)
---
Thank you for everything you do, Peter.

– Roy

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

| | Peter, I understand that organizers don’t have unlimited resources. I understand that sometimes, we have to make tough calls. I understand that big dreams take time to achieve. But I will _never_ understand how anyone could look me in the eyes and tell me that my home state – and everyone living there – isn’t “worth” fighting for. And I’m damn sure not listening to it in 2026.** [**_It takes real work to win tough fights. But it’s work we _know_ how to do, and I believe we can do it. clean_body: | ~ | | Peter, I understand that organizers don’t have unlimited resources. I understand that sometimes, we have to make tough calls. I understand that big dreams take time to achieve. But I will never understand how anyone could look me in the eyes and tell me that my home state – and everyone living there – isn’t “worth” fighting for. Still, people always ask why we’re so invested in organizing across Florida. They claim that Florida is too red, too far gone, too deep under the thumb of the far-right fascists like Ron DeSantis, and that we can’t “afford” to fight back. If I’d listened to that kind of defeatism in 2022, I wouldn’t be writing to you today as the first Gen Z member of Congress. And I’m damn sure not listening to it in 2026. ~ ~ | | ~ Thanks to people like you, chipping in spare change and sometimes digging even deeper, we’ve gained ground in Florida. That’s why they’re trying to rig the Congressional maps against Democrats. This state is in play, and you won’t catch me on the sidelines when everything from our education to our democracy to our planet’s survival is at stake. Now, I’m not gonna sugarcoat what we’re really up against. It’s true that Floridians have been subjected to far-right policies for years, and that it’s caused real suffering. It’s true that billionaire weirdos have been funding fascism here for even longer. But that’s exactly why we have to organize and fight back. I’m proud to have earned the support of a broad coalition who believe in our vision for accountable, people-first leadership.**So far, we’ve received endorsements and distinctions from:**
* The Houston Chronicle
* Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus
* Secular Houston
* Progressive Voters Network
* Harris County Young Democrats
* Area 5 Democrats
* Mothers Against Greg Abbott
* Moms Demand Action (Gun Sense Candidate _Designation_)

Friend,
My name is Sandra Cameron. I'm Daniel's mom, and I want to take a few minutes of your time because _there are some things only a mother can tell you about a man._
I raised Daniel in Elizabethtown, Kentucky. Before he ever won an election, before he ever argued a case, before he ever set foot in the attorney general's office, Daniel was my little boy working alongside his father at our coffee shop.
**Daniel has always been hardworking.** He earned a scholarship on his own merits and went to the University of Louisville to play football and study law. But more than anything, he was a son who never once gave me reason to doubt the values we instilled in him at home. I can’t tell you how much peace and joy that brings as a parent.
I spent my career as an educator. I have seen what it looks like when a young person has genuine character, and I have seen what it looks like when they don't.
**Daniel has it. **
**Not because someone taught him to perform it, but because he chose it, day after day, long before anyone was watching. **
When Daniel became the first black American independently elected to a standalone statewide office in Kentucky's history, I was so proud. But not for the reason people might expect. I was proud because I knew who he was in private, and I knew Americans had just seen what I had always had.
**That man is now running for the United States Senate. And the May 19 primary is just weeks away.**
**I won't pretend the race is easy. My son is up against well-funded opponents, and the attacks on Daniel have been serious. Our ability to answer them and carry his message to every corner of this commonwealth depends on the support of people like you.**
[_**I am asking you, as his mother, and as someone who has watched him his entire life, to please make a contribution today. Whatever you can give will make a real difference.**_](https://eot.cameronforkentucky.com/f/a/FrzqLwmX3iiJhkeXT5QA4w~~/AAAHURA~/LJrJvuax_St2tc3d67cxFB9X-Krsc71xhnS5Y8Ahkera-7bqgiPUEQQRmKlVpM1LD7nWfQP0Rkx4lOaFf4pkYdAorxUT28OcIYTaJyaAmV2CI8by-qpJ30-ZjntNIfFfVVW7lPAmHt6_k-qY230D2tsmxU6usPmwKvgRXwQVNQM2VUHY1Dzt2jHkYlz8JYCyU-22lCI3sA6CrVoG_wHgvfCtVKu5_MqzhgYIUDVoYsiBKEb-qNXt7ktV14m50aYATe1nuqhr0Z0h_5RsqYpiSQ~~)
**I love my son. And I love what he stands for.** I have known him longer than anyone, and I could not be prouder of the man he is. So trust me when I say, _Daniel is exactly who Americans need in Washington. _
Thank you,
Sandra Cameron

body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor

In honor of Marathon Monday, I’ve been thinking a lot about what it takes
to keep going, especially when something really matters.

I’ve run more than 40 marathons in my life, but one stands out.

Almost a decade ago, I ran the Boston Marathon while I was eight months
pregnant.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4121?t=1001&akid=1601%2E181023%2E1FOf7L ]Jocelyn Benson running the Boston Marathon, eight months pregnant.

It wasn’t about speed or setting a record. I knew I had to take it slower,
listen to my body, and focus on finishing. And crossing that finish line
with my husband biking by my side meant everything.

It’s a reminder that I keep with me on the campaign trail. Strength isn’t
always about how fast you go – it’s about showing up, staying steady, and
refusing to give up.

And this campaign is a lot like a marathon.

It takes discipline, resilience, and willingness to keep going even when
things get tough. There are moments of momentum, and moments where you
have to dig a little deeper, but the only way to get there is to keep
moving forward.

We know this race won’t be easy. After Donald Trump’s 2024 win, Michigan
is a top target, and outside money is already pouring in.

But we’re building something strong enough to go the distance — a campaign
powered by people, not special interests.

So in the spirit of Marathon Monday, I’m asking:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4121?t=1002&akid=1601%2E181023%2E1FOf7L ]Will you chip in $26.20 or another amount today to help us keep moving
forward and building the kind of campaign it takes to win?

Thank you for being part of this team,

Jocelyn

---
| |
---
| | **Dear Friends,** It is with a heavy heart that our family invites you to join us in saying a final farewell to my father, Brigadier General (Ret.) James Emory Mace.
---
|
---
| **Funeral Service** Thursday, April 23, 2026 | 5:00 PM Eastern Summerall Chapel, The Citadel 171 Moultrie St, Charleston, SC 29409 [obits.jhenrystuhr.com/bg-j-emory-mace-us-army-ret](https://nancymace.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f826f615915b06bdee33acac8&id=9633dc8721&e=ddc57b5ede)
---
|
---
| We will gather in the chapel where my parents were married in 1964 and we will honor a South Carolina born and bred war hero. Dad was born in Hampton County, South Carolina and gave 28 years of his life to the United States Army, retiring as an Infantry Brigadier General. His valor in Vietnam earned him some of our nation’s highest honors: the Distinguished Service Cross with “V” Device, Distinguished Service Medal, Silver Star, Legion of Merit, multiple Bronze Stars with “V” devices for valor, the Army Commendation Medal, and the Purple Heart. He authored the first-ever Ranger field manual and transformed the Ranger Training Brigade. While still with us, he was the most decorated graduate of The Citadel.
---

|
---
| [obits.jhenrystuhr.com/bg-j-emory-mace-us-army-ret](https://nancymace.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f826f615915b06bdee33acac8&id=0d76d0fb73&e=ddc57b5ede)
---
| He showed me strength. He taught me what it means to be unbreakable. There are no words large enough for what he meant to me. “Well done, good and faithful servant.” — Matthew 25:23 **With love,** Nancy R. Mace

| | | | | | Peter,

**Tomorrow could be the day the Senate Judiciary Committee votes on House Bill 1793.

** Your calls and emails have already made a real difference and forced the committee to take this bill seriously.

Now we must keep the pressure on until we get Campus Carry over the finish line!

HB 1793 prohibits public colleges and universities from banning the possession or carrying of firearms and non-lethal self-defense tools on campus.

**It ends the dangerous practice of gun-free zones that leave students, faculty, and visitors completely defenseless.**

Sponsored by Pledge Champion Representative Sam Farrington, this bill restores the constitutional right of law-abiding adults to protect themselves where they live and learn.

Some committee members are still considering weakening amendments that would gut the heart of the bill and leave campuses vulnerable. We cannot let that happen.

# [America Needs More Veteran Entrepreneurs](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4399133&post_id=194792793&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk0NzkyNzkzLCJpYXQiOjE3NzY2OTA4MDAsImV4cCI6MTc3OTI4MjgwMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQzOTkxMzMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RXGYTLRZmj9uJha46VrhEo3_yo7zi8OdTMa9zdVdx94)
### Veterans built the postwar American economy. We need to do that again.
| | [Patrick J. Murphy](https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa) and [Steven Berry](https://substack.com/@stevenberry10)
---
| Apr 20
---
| [](https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa)| | [](https://substack.com/@stevenberry10)
---|---|---

| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4399133&post_id=194792793&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk0NzkyNzkzLCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc3NjY5MDgwMCwiZXhwIjoxNzc5MjgyODAwLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItNDM5OTEzMyIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.gTppMEkGpEgmKUCYDS4lG5fz09CoyAg4lzX4LmwlgfU&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/patrickmurphypa/p/america-needs-more-veteran-entrepreneurs?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

After World War II, [nearly half of all American small businesses were founded by veterans](https://substack.com/redirect/636cdf48-b990-48b1-8877-4ca21b31eec6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Men who had managed supply chains under fire and made life-or-death decisions at 22 years old came home, took the GI Bill, found a storefront, and built something. Sam Walton opened his first Walmart in 1962. A decade later, Fred Smith came back from two combat tours in Vietnam and founded FedEx. Phil Knight, fresh out of the Army Reserve, started what would become Nike. The American economy of the postwar decades ran, in no small part, on the operational instincts of people who had been trained to execute under pressure.
The number of veterans starting their own small business is now [less than 5%](https://substack.com/redirect/b5c46a1e-bff2-4a3f-a10c-b8ea19527936?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We think about that gap a lot. Both of us are Army Veterans, one came home from Baghdad with a Bronze Star and $322 in his bank account, the other is now a banker who has spent his career watching capital flow toward the people best positioned to deploy it. From where we each sit, the same problem looks different but leads to the same conclusion: America is leaving an enormous amount on the table by treating its veterans as recipients of charity rather than as drivers of economic growth.
The culture of honoring veterans runs deep in America. The problem is that honoring someone and investing in them are not the same thing, and we have gotten very good at the former while largely avoiding the latter. It shows up as a handshake, a discount at a hardware store, a "thank you for your service" that functions as a conversation-ender rather than a conversation-starter. Veterans get placed in jobs below their capability and told to be grateful for the opportunity. What rarely happens is someone looking at a 28-year-old who spent four years managing a 40-person team in a combat zone and thinking: this person knows how to build something.

The military produces exactly what high-growth companies need and almost never find. It's not because the military has some magic formula, but because it has no choice. An Army captain who manages by committee gets people killed. A logistics officer with unclear accountability loses the mission. A JAG lawyer running a brigade operational law team in Baghdad doesn't get to tell anyone he needs another week. The skills that make someone effective in uniform -- disciplined execution, calm under pressure, leading people through ambiguity toward a clear objective -- are the same skills that determine whether a company makes it past year three.
We have a phrase for this in the military: [hire for trait, train for skill](https://substack.com/redirect/69e7df6d-68d4-4e3f-9d67-a7dc73eea4ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The idea is that execution capacity, judgment under pressure, and the willingness to own a result are things you can't teach in an onboarding session, so you select for them first and build everything else around them. Most of the corporate world does the opposite. They hire for credential and pedigree and assume execution will follow.
This is why the convergence happening right now between the public and private sectors matters so much and why veterans need to be at the center of it.
The national security challenges America faces today are concrete and urgent. The U.S. is 50 to 100 percent net import reliant on critical minerals. China has nine industrial robots deployed for every one in the United States. It takes roughly twelve years for America to manufacture a war-ready jet, ship, or tank. These are not just defense problems -- they are industrial problems, supply chain problems, capital allocation problems, and solving them will require the same combination of operational discipline and entrepreneurial risk-taking that built the postwar American economy in the first place. That work doesn't get done by a Pentagon budget line or a congressional hearing. It gets done by people who know how to build things under pressure and move faster than the bureaucracy that surrounds them. That is a job description that fits a lot of veterans. It fits almost no one else as well.
JP Morgan's [Security and Resiliency Initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/d06889ba-e905-4721-b47e-05de04ca439c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (SRI) -- a $1.5 trillion commitment to finance and invest in industries critical to national security -- is one signal that the private sector understands the stakes. The focus areas map almost perfectly onto where veteran operators have the most to offer: supply chain resilience, defense and aerospace, energy independence, and frontier technology. These are industries that reward the kind of thinking that gets drilled into you during military service. Not the polish of a pitch deck, but the ability to see a complex system, identify where it's fragile, and fix it.
That instinct shows up at every level of scale. Take [Brecourt Solutions](https://substack.com/redirect/77281f9f-f9a2-4600-bf53-c64a41a513fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Founded by a former Navy SEAL, Brecourt keeps communities and institutions safe by identifying and interdicting active shooters in real time. In the process of building that capability, the team ran headfirst into a different problem: the fragility of the drone component supply chain. So they did what veteran operators are trained to do: identify the point of failure and take ownership of fixing it. Today, Brecourt is not only deploying systems to protect lives in real time, but also building the domestic manufacturing network needed to produce critical drone components at scale in the United States, enabling an entire category of companies to operate with greater speed and resilience.
* * *
We've both spent time thinking about why the veteran entrepreneurship rate collapsed so dramatically from where it was after World War II. Part of it is structural -- the GI Bill was originally designed to help veterans go to school and buy homes, not start companies. Part of it is cultural -- somewhere along the way, "supporting veterans" became synonymous with employment assistance rather than business formation. And part of it is that veterans themselves are sometimes the last ones to see their own transferable value, because the military doesn't spend much time translating what you did into the language civilians understand.
What the data shows is that veteran-owned businesses tend to outlast their non-veteran counterparts -- roughly [55 to 57 percent survive past five years](https://substack.com/redirect/4a569b26-5805-427f-95b8-552e9b8c8001?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), compared to about 50 percent for the general population. They also hire other veterans at higher rates, creating a multiplier effect across the workforce. The business case for veteran entrepreneurship isn't a charity argument. Veteran-owned businesses generate over $1 trillion in annual revenue and employ millions of Americans.
The industries that matter most for American competitiveness over the next decade -- critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity, defense technology -- require people who understand both the mission and the market. Veterans who have worked at the intersection of national security and operations are not a niche talent pool for these problems. They're a natural fit.
The sea of goodwill Americans extend to veterans is wide and also insufficient. Goodwill without capital, mentorship, and a serious ecosystem for veteran business formation doesn't build the next Nike or FedEx.
We send these people overseas to defend our country. The least we can do is support them when they come home.

_Patrick J. Murphy is the Executive Director of the Geopolitical Unit at Hilco Global. A combat veteran, former U.S. Congressman, and the 32nd Undersecretary of the Army, he deployed to Baghdad with the 82nd Airborne in 2003 and was the first Iraq War veteran elected to Congress. He is a nonresidential fellow at the Wharton School._
_Steve Berry is a Vice President and Banker at J.P. Morgan Private Bank, where he advises veteran business owners, financial professionals, and high-net-worth individuals on wealth management, capital allocation, and investment strategy. A former U.S. Army Special Operations officer and Bronze Star recipient, he served with the 95th Civil Affairs Brigade (Airborne) in Eastern Europe and Afghanistan before building a career at the intersection of finance and national security._

name: Democrats.org
subject: We’re making them nervous
body:
Alarm bells are ringing for Republicans...
---
Derek, **_265 races.**_ That’s right: We’ve won or overperformed in _265 out of 296_ key elections since Trump took office — nearly 90%. I am proud to honor this local hero.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129797398/615604201/-153530995?refcode=EM_F_260417hero_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_LOGO&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NzgxYjRmMS1iYTNjLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=38V_OvNNPET5R7l-CjUholBqwMsahttD4FCMk2sq_ss=) Peter,

I am so proud to announce that the House has passed my legislation to name the Collinwood neighborhood Post Office in Cleveland in honor of Tech Sergeant Alma Gladys Minter. The bill now heads to the Senate for a vote.

Minter was a long-time Cleveland resident who valiantly served her country as a member of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II. The “Six Triple Eight” was the first and only all-Black Women’s Army Corps unit to serve overseas during the war.

The women of the Six Triple Eight served with courage and excellence, yet far too many never lived to see their country recognize them. The Six Triple Eight was awarded the Congressional Gold Medal by Congress in 2022 for their work helping to clear a backlog of over 17 million pieces of mail in Europe.

**Instead of bowing out when faced with a challenge, Minter rose to the occasion to deliver for her country. I am so happy that this bill is a step closer to becoming law.**

[**Despite the Republican led chaos in Washington, we are still getting wins where we can and honoring local heroes. Please help us continue to fight to move our nation forward, not back, by pitching in $5 to my re-election campaign today.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129797401/615604204/-153530995?refcode=EM_F_260417hero_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_L1&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NzgxYjRmMS1iYTNjLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=38V_OvNNPET5R7l-CjUholBqwMsahttD4FCMk2sq_ss=)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
